title: The 1988-2024 ALOHA oxygen loss has a nutrient ratio change on density 26.4-26.6
abstract: We test a nutrient constraint on the outcrop explanation of North Pacific oxygen loss. Frozen ALOHA annual results show that AOU rose by 21.11 umol/kg on density 26.4-26.6 between 1988-1996 and 2009-2024. Nitrate plus nitrite rose by 1.927 and phosphate by 0.1562 umol/kg. Their increment ratio is 12.34, with a conditional year-block interval of 11.10-14.15. The change in N minus 16 P is -0.572 umol/kg. Its change relative to lighter classes is -0.571 (-0.713 to -0.427), and relative to denser classes is -0.644 (-0.967 to -0.336). These contrasts cancel common additive nutrient offsets. Later epochs also show a change after the documented 2000-2004 laboratory transition, but that later test cannot exclude a common gain-and-offset correction. Longer water age with fixed preformed composition and 16:1 nutrient release cannot produce the main nutrient residual. Source composition, transport, release ratios or other errors must contribute. This does not establish denitrification or reject the outcrop mechanism. The work uses published annual aggregates, short conditional resampling intervals and exploratory band choices. Code, source hashes, new statistics and reproduction instructions are included.

display.caption: The nutrient residual falls near the AOU peak. Vertical controls remove common additive offsets. Intervals use correlated year blocks.
